ExampleDefinition.ShowcaseDescription: An interactive thematic map of Europe. Countries are shaded by total population (darker means more people), and each city is a bubble sized by its population and coloured by its urban primacy (the city's share of its country's population) via a ColorMap. Demonstrates filled polygon rendering, a bubble series with a ColorMap and a custom value provider, geographic projection, dual legends, tooltips and interactive filtering. The map uses the Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area projection (EPSG:3035) used by Eurostat for Europe.
ExampleDefinition.ToolTipDescription: A population map of Europe: countries shaded by population, with cities sized by population and coloured by urban primacy.
ExampleDefinition.Description:
This example is an interactive thematic map of Europe built entirely from geographic data.
Countries are drawn with a custom [b]FilledPolygonRenderableSeries[/b] that renders filled polygons, shaded by total population so that darker regions hold more people.
Each city is a bubble drawn by a [b]FastBubbleRenderableSeries[/b], encoding two independent values at once. The bubble [b]size[/b] is the city's population (sized by area), and the bubble [b]colour[/b] is its [b]urban primacy[/b] (the city's share of its country's total population), applied through a ColorMap and a custom value provider. A large, bright bubble is a metropolis that dominates its country; a large, deep-blue bubble is a big city in a populous, polycentric one.
Every coordinate (country polygons and city points) is projected from longitude and latitude to the Lambert Azimuthal Equal-Area projection (EPSG:3035, the standard Eurostat projection for Europe), giving Europe its familiar shape with Scandinavia at the top and Spain and Turkey at the lower corners. The [b]AspectRatioViewportManager[/b] keeps the projected map undistorted.
Two legends explain the encodings: a country population colour key on the left, and a city key on the right with graduated circles for population and a colour bar for urban primacy. Hovering over a bubble shows the city name, country, population and primacy.
[b][i] The following interactions are possible:[/i][/b]
- [b][MouseWheel][/b] to zoom in and out - Click and drag the [b][Left Mouse Button][/b] to pan - Double-click the [b][Left Mouse Button][/b] to zoom to the full extent - Hover the mouse over a city to show its tooltip
[b][i] Toolbar actions: [/i][/b]
- Open the [b]Min City Population[/b] flyout and drag the slider to filter out smaller cities - Open the [b]Aspect Ratio[/b] flyout to change how the map is kept undistorted (mode and ratio)
